% behavior-by-stage / alignment-by-aspect). Both are two-column figure* floats;

% ACL (set FONT_SCALE = 1.14 in plot_paper_figures.py to cancel that out).
% Generated by experiments/profile_expansion/figures/plot_paper_figures.py

\begin{figure*}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figs/overall_model_performance.pdf}
    \caption{
        \textbf{Overall model performance.}
        Bars show mean scores and error bars indicate 95\% bootstrap confidence
        intervals across profiles. Angel achieves the highest Simulation Diversity
        and Behavior Diversity while maintaining strong Profile Alignment. Because
        the three metrics occupy different parts of the $0$--$1$ range, all three
        y-axes are truncated for visualization, as marked by the break on each
        axis.
    }
    \label{fig:overall_model_performance}
\end{figure*}

\begin{figure*}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figs/stage_aspect_performance.pdf}
    \caption{
        \textbf{Stage- and aspect-level model performance.}
        \textbf{(a)} Simulation Diversity across interview stages, on a zero
        baseline.
        \textbf{(b)} Behavior Diversity across interview stages and
        \textbf{(c)} Profile Alignment across profile aspects; both axes are
        linear but truncated below the lowest score, as marked by the break on
        the axis, so that the low-scoring risk stages remain visible.
        Bars show mean scores and error bars indicate 95\% bootstrap confidence
        intervals. Angel achieves consistently high Simulation Diversity and
        Behavior Diversity across stages -- most visibly on the risk-assessment
        stages -- while maintaining competitive Profile Alignment.
    }
    \label{fig:stage_aspect_performance}
\end{figure*}

\begin{figure*}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figs/diversity_by_runs.pdf}
    \caption{
        \textbf{Diversity as a function of the number of runs.}
        Lines show mean scores across profiles, and shaded regions indicate
        95\% bootstrap confidence intervals. Each point pools that many runs per
        profile.
        \textbf{(a)} Simulation Diversity generally decreases as more runs are
        pooled and gradually plateaus. Angel maintains the highest scores, whereas
        Eeyore remains lowest.
        \textbf{(b)} Behavior Diversity changes less substantially with the number
        of runs, with Angel maintaining the highest scores throughout.
    }
    \label{fig:diversity_by_runs}
\end{figure*}

% NOTE: this figure plots the MEASURED run-4 fixed-attribute values. It is not a
% restyle of the fixed_attr_vs_{simulation,behavior}_diversity.pdf figures from fixed_attributes/plot_fixed_attr_diversity_four_metrics.py,
% which were produced by that script's --illustrative path (every score multiplied
% by 1 - alpha*(k-1)/21, alpha=0.30 and 0.55 for Eeyore) and therefore show a
% decline that is not in the data. Wording below follows the measured trends.

\begin{figure*}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figs/diversity_by_fixed_attributes.pdf}
    \caption{
        \textbf{Diversity as a function of the number of fixed profile
        attributes.}
        Lines show mean scores across the variant profiles at each constraint
        level $K$, and shaded regions indicate 95\% bootstrap confidence
        intervals.
        \textbf{(a)} Simulation Diversity decreases modestly as more attributes
        are fixed for three of the four systems (Angel $-10\%$, Roleplay-doh
        $-13\%$, Patient-psi $-7\%$ from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}22$), while Eeyore shows
        no decline from an already low baseline. Angel maintains the highest
        scores across all values of $K$.
        \textbf{(b)} Behavior Diversity is largely insensitive to $K$: every
        system stays within $4\%$ of its $K{=}1$ value, with Angel highest at
        nearly every constraint level.
    }
    \label{fig:diversity_fixed_attributes}
\end{figure*}
